name: California Lowball
description: California Lowball (also known as Ace-to-Five Single Draw) is a Five Card Draw Poker variant where the lowest hand wins using ace-to-five ranking. Aces are always low, straights and flushes don't count. Best hand is A-2-3-4-5 (wheel). Often played with a joker as a wild card.

overview.description: California Lowball (also known as Ace-to-Five Single Draw) is a Five Card Draw Poker variant where the lowest hand wins using ace-to-five ranking. Aces are always low, straights and flushes don't count. Best hand is A-2-3-4-5 (wheel). Often played with a joker as a wild card.

history.origins: California Lowball emerged as a popular poker variant in California card rooms. The ace-to-five ranking system became the standard for lowball games on the American West Coast.
timeline: Early-mid 20th century: Lowball poker variants developed in California
Mid-late 20th century: Became staple of California card rooms
Modern era: Still played in card rooms and home games; online versions available
history.cultural: California Lowball was once a staple of California card rooms, particularly in the Bay Area. While less common in modern casinos, it remains popular in home games and is offered by some online poker sites.
history.evolution: The game evolved from Five Card Draw with the simple inversion of hand rankings - lowest hand wins instead of highest. The ace-to-five system (A-2-3-4-5 as best hand) became standard. The addition of a joker as a wild card (representing the lowest missing rank) is a common modern variation.

setup.players: Two to six players. In formal games the dealer posts a small blind and the next two players to the dealer's left each post a big blind equal to the minimum bet; alternatively the game may be played with an ante from each player. Everyone is dealt five cards face down.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck, optionally plus one joker (called the 'fitter'). If joker is used, it represents the lowest rank not present in the hand.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 5 cards face down. Played with blinds (dealer posts small blind, next two players post big blinds) or with antes.

rules.objective: Form the lowest possible 5-card hand using ace-to-five ranking. Win the pot by having the best (lowest) hand at showdown or by making all other players fold.
rules.gameplay: Five Card Draw format with one drawing round. Each player dealt 5 cards face down. First betting round (begins left of blinds/antes). Surviving players may discard any number of cards (seldom more than one in practice) and receive replacements. Second betting round. Showdown: lowest hand wins using ace-to-five ranking. Aces always low; straights and flushes don't count. Hands compared by highest card first (7-5-4-3-2 beats 7-6-3-2-A because 5 < 6).
keyRules: Straights and flushes do not count
A-2-3-4-5 is the best possible hand
Compare highest cards first when ranking hands
Optional joker acts as lowest missing rank

strategy.basic: Aim for five unpaired cards with as many low cards as possible. A-2-3-4-5 (wheel) is the nuts. Drawing more than one card is risky because you'll make a pair about half the time. Generally, draw only one card or stand pat.
strategy.intermediate: Position matters - acting last gives information about opponents' hand strength. Consider pot odds when deciding whether to draw. With a very strong hand like 8-high or better, consider representing weakness to induce bets. Pay attention to how many cards opponents draw - standing pat or drawing one suggests a strong hand.
strategy.advanced: Bluffing is effective because opponents can't see your cards. Representing strength by standing pat with a weak hand can win pots. Conversely, slow-playing a wheel (A-2-3-4-5) can induce bluffs. The 'betting sevens' rule (if used) affects strategy - checking with 7-low or better is dangerous as you may lose eligibility for post-draw bets.
tips: Never draw more than one card if you can avoid it
A wheel (A-2-3-4-5) is the absolute nuts - play it strongly
Standing pat (drawing zero cards) represents a made hand
Drawing one card suggests you have four low cards to a good hand
If joker is used, it adds flexibility - 4-card hands become playable
Be aware of 'betting sevens' rule if playing that variation
Bluffing is more effective in lowball than in many poker variants

scoring.description: Ace-to-five lowball ranking: Best hand is A-2-3-4-5 (wheel). Then A-2-3-4-6, A-2-3-5-6, etc. Compare highest cards first, then second highest, etc. Paired cards are bad - any hand with five different ranks beats any hand with a pair. With joker: represents lowest missing rank (e.g., 8-6-4-A-joker = 8-6-4-2-A).
